Sam Patel (SimpliBank): Hey team — we're onboarding BYOK for Redwood Private. A few questions about Azure Key Vault setup and rotation requirements.
Alex Kim (support): Welcome Sam! Can you list the high-level goals? e.g., HSM vs software keys, rotation cadence, audit sinks.
Sam Patel (SimpliBank): HSM keys required. We want monthly key rotation (automated), audit logs stored in our subscription for 1 year, and envelope encryption for object blobs. Also need guidance on RBAC so our ops team can provision keys without granting too much.
Priya Rao (security): Quick note — for envelope encryption we only need Redwood to perform wrapKey/unwrapKey ops via a service principal or managed identity; Redwood never stores the private key material. Also we'll need proof of diagnostic logs + retention during onboarding.
Jordan Lee (devex): For RBAC, recommend two roles: 1) Key authors (importKey, create, update) for your key ops team; 2) Runtime role for Redwood (get, wrapKey, unwrapKey, list). Avoid giving Redwood `delete`/`purge`/`backup` unless you want us to handle lifecycle.
Alex Kim (support): Example minimal Key permissions (Key operations): `get`, `wrapKey`, `unwrapKey`, `list`. If you plan to rotate by creating new versions and allow Redwood to switch to new version, also include `get` on key versions.
Sam Patel (SimpliBank): How do we automate rotation and ensure Redwood picks up new version without manual steps?
Priya Rao (security): Two options:
- You rotate by creating a new key version in KV. Redwood polls on startup or you can trigger a config refresh via the Console/API to point to the new version.
- Better: enable version-agnostic key reference (use key identifier root without version) and allow Redwood to call `get` to resolve latest version. We recommend a canary window after rotation to validate outputs before forcing traffic.
Alex Kim (support): For diagnostics/audit logs — we need `Microsoft.KeyVault/locations/vaults/providers/diagnosticSettings/write` to set up export if you want Redwood to help configure it. Otherwise you can configure and send `AzureDiagnostics` and `AuditEvent` to Event Hub / Log Analytics / Storage. Sample CLI:
````
az monitor diagnostic-settings create \
  --resource-id /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/<kv> \
  --name redwood-diagnostics \
  --logs '[{"category":"AuditEvent","enabled":true}]' \
  --workspace /subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/microsoft.operationalinsights/workspaces/<la>
````
Sam Patel (SimpliBank): Nice. Any specific retention / log fields we rely on for compliance checks?
Priya Rao (security): We look for `OperationName`, `ResultType`, `ResultSignature`, and `CorrelationId` for tracing unwrap/wrap calls. 1 year retention is fine; 3 years for regulated customers.
Jordan Lee (devex): For envelope encryption, verify the flow locally:
1) Redwood requests get+wrapKey to encrypt a random data key.
2) Redwood encrypts payload with the data key locally.
3) Redwood stores encrypted data key (envelope) alongside object.
Recommend a simple test harness: run a small blob write/read with `wrapKey` and `unwrapKey` and assert successful decrypt.
Alex Kim (support): If you're importing keys (you said HSM), will you use `import` (bring-your-own-key) or Azure Key Vault HSM import? Remember imported HSM keys must be in a supported format and you may need to submit to HSM with import protection.
Sam Patel (SimpliBank): We'll import via our HSM appliance, but might need Redwood to validate the imported key's attributes (key_ops, key_size, curve). Can support check those automatically?
Alex Kim (support): Yes — we can run a validation job during onboarding: check `key.kid` format, `key_ops` includes `wrapKey`/`unwrapKey`, `kty` matches policy (RSA-HSM or EC-HSM), and `attributes.enabled==true`. We'll run the following Az check:
````
az keyvault key show --vault-name <kv> --name <key-name>
az keyvault key list-versions --vault-name <kv> --name <key-name>
````
Priya Rao (security): Also confirm there are no legacy access policies granting broad permissions to `Microsoft.KeyVault/*` for non-admins. Use Azure RBAC (Azure role assignments) over legacy access policies whenever possible.
Sam Patel (SimpliBank): Last thing — rotation notifications. Can Redwood notify us if key unwrap fails (e.g., rotated and Redwood still using old version)?
Jordan Lee (devex): Yes, Redwood has alerting hooks. We can create a webhook integration to your ops channel and alert on `unwrap` errors with the `key_id` and `api_request_id`. We also provide trace logs in the Console per-request.
Alex Kim (support): Next steps for onboarding:
- Share KV resource id and a readonly principal for validation (we will only call `get` & `list` during validation unless you authorize config changes).
- Share the key name(s) and indicate import vs generated.
- Optionally provide an Event Hub / Log Analytics workspace id if you want us to assist with diagnostics setup.
Sam Patel (SimpliBank): I'll share the resource id and create a managed identity for Redwood with `Key Vault Crypto User` + `get/wrap/unwrap/list` on the key, and will open a ticket if we want Redwood to set diagnostic settings.
Priya Rao (security): Thanks — once we validate, we'll provide a short onboarding checklist and a compliance snapshot (permissions, sample audit events, sample unwrap calls).
Alex Kim (support): Sounds good. Tag me when you drop the resource id, Sam, and we'll kick off the validation run. :thumbsup: 
Sam Patel (SimpliBank): Thanks all, will do by EOD.
